rationale: Round 0 built and ran cleanly with no ICE fallback, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up across all seven passes while keeping cost weights bounded. SUB is weighted aggressively (high security, minimal cost/risk) since instruction substitution is nearly free and this 1.8 KB binary has little size headroom to lose. FLA and BCF get high security/diversity weights because the largest functions (main, ReadList, QuickSort at ~340-505 bytes) have enough control flow to flatten and bogus-condition-protect meaningfully, but their RuntimeCost weights are held at 0.4 since QuickSort/BubbleSort are hot loops and unbounded flattening would hurt. SPLIT is kept as a cheap diversity amplifier that composes with FLA. IBR gets solid security weighting to break static patching of the sort's branch-dense code. ICALL and IGV diversify indirect calls and global ordering across the three translation units (benchmark, readlist, sort), raising cross-module analysis cost, with CorrectnessRisk capped at 0.3 so the selector avoids these on fragile recursion in QuickSort. Overall the table biases every pass toward application on feature-favored functions while moderate cost weights keep the selector from forcing passes onto size- or latency-critical code paths.
